note: Iluka Supply Agreement (Oct 2022): binding contract for 30,500 t of contained TREO within a 20-30% xenotime concentrate (total_tonnes is contained TREO, not concentrate mass); Iluka takes 100% of product up to a 5,500 tpa TREO maximum with right of first refusal on excess. Delivery by road from first concentrate (2028). RISK: certain conditions precedent (NTU financing/FID, Iluka financial close) passed their satisfaction dates as at Sep 2025, entitling either party to terminate; neither has, and extensions are under discussion (NTU DFS pp.5, 91-92). Corroborated by Iluka AR25 p.9: 'the prospect of offtake under our existing agreement with Northern Minerals was also strengthened by support from the Australian and US governments for the development of the Browns Range deposit'.

Existing stake: in October 2022 Iluka invested A$20M in Northern Minerals - A$5M for 125 million ordinary shares (still held; fair value A$3.8M at 31 Dec 2025) and a A$15M convertible note that matured 31 Dec 2024 and was redeemed in 2025 for A$18.5M incl. interest (AR25 note 5(c), p.112). Conditional further commitment: per the NTU DFS (p.86) Iluka may subscribe for ~A$53M of additional equity post-FID via placement and put/call options, subject to positive FID, secured project funding, Iluka due diligence and continuation of the Supply Agreement - that tranche remains PLANNED.

AR25 p.21: 'Wimmera's rare earths are an important potential future feedstock for the Eneabba refinery'; p.9: 'a potential multi decade source of light and heavy rare earths'. High confidence this is the intended pathway; project remains in DFS. The ~15 ktpa / 25+ year volume from Iluka's refinery feed scenarios is NOT in AR25 and is held on the project record against an unverified placeholder source (annual_tonnes left null here).

Heavy mineral concentrate requires further processing in the Northern Territory or Western Australia; specific refinery not publicly established. Insufficient evidence to assert Fingerboards -> Eneabba.

15-year offtake structure covering the four magnet rare earths announced April 2026; USAR names future Serra Verde concentrates as planned oxide-production feedstock. No evidence material has yet physically flowed.
Inferred from USAR's stated integrated mining-to-magnets strategy; internal flow within the USAR platform.
Inferred from USAR's stated integrated mining-to-magnets strategy; internal flow within the USAR platform.

Separated oxides -> metals/alloys -> magnets is a functional dependency only; no offtake, metallisation or magnet-production counterparty identified. AR25: offtake discussions with commercial customers ongoing, priority is binding agreements on pricing independent of the Asian Metal Index (p.9, p.31); metallisation feasibility study advanced in 2025 and will conclude in 2026, with electrolytic cell development with technology partners (p.9, p.21, p.29). Earlier: FID release (2022, p.2) named metallisation as a potential future step; NTU DFS (Fig 41, p.74) shows a 'potential Iluka metallisation plant (study in progress)' with ex-China magnet producers / Western OEMs as the intended market.

The refinery will be fed initially from Iluka's own Eneabba monazite/xenotime stockpile, giving an indicative nine-year refinery life on the stockpile alone with project NPV > A$500M under that conservative scenario (FID 2022, p.2). Owned feed - not dependent on any third-party mine. AR25 p.57: stockpile feed supports up to 18 ktpa contained REO into the plant and 16.0 ktpa REO output; Iluka's 2026 incentive targets 15 ktpa REO feed in the first year of operation (commissioning 2027).

Same refinery and already in Iluka's hands, so a Browns Range disruption does not stop Eneabba producing. Caveat: the stockpile is monazite-dominant (LREE-rich) with a xenotime component; its Dy/Tb contribution relative to Browns Range's concentrate is not quantified in this source, so it is an alternative for refinery throughput more than for heavy rare-earth volume.

Australian Government risk-sharing arrangement under the Critical Minerals Facility, administered by Export Finance Australia: non-recourse loan to Iluka Eneabba Pty Ltd secured against the refinery, BBSY + 3%, term up to 16 years expiring 2038, repayments from project completion. Originally A$1,050M + A$200M overrun (FID 2022; Iluka equity A$200M on 1:3 basis, royalty to Iluka up to A$81M/yr capped at A$900M). AR25 (pp.12, 127-128): facility increased to A$1,650M in Feb 2025 (Iluka cash contribution rising to A$414M); the additional A$400M tranche is subject to securing offtake satisfactory to the Australian Government and drawable only after the initial A$1,450M is used; A$609.7M drawn at 31 Dec 2025 at 7.8% effective; A$150M overrun facility (50% EFA / 50% Iluka) undrawn. Debt, not equity - drawn and in force, hence OBSERVED.

Rare-earth concentrate supply agreement finalised in 2025 between Iluka and Lindian Resources, 'securing 10% of the refinery's capacity feedstock for 15 years, with options to significantly increase the volume and duration of the contract' (AR25 p.9, p.53). Kangankunde is a neodymium/praseodymium (light rare earth) source, so this diversifies Eneabba's feed but does not substitute for Browns Range Dy/Tb. Tonnage not disclosed.
Agreement announced April 2026 for Serra Verde to combine with USA Rare Earth; not modelled as completed ownership.
Uses the same downstream refining infrastructure (Eneabba), so a Browns Range disruption could be mitigated without a new refining pathway.
Already producing Dy/Tb-bearing material, unlike the Australian projects; relies on a separate (USAR) downstream pathway rather than Eneabba.
Significant potential Dy/Tb output in an allied jurisdiction, but downstream pathway is unresolved; that uncertainty should lower its ranking, not be hidden.
